consensus_summary: Swine symbolize ritual/moral uncleanness and the profane — those who scorn or trample holy things (Matt 7:6) and apostates who return to filth (2 Pet 2:22) — rooted in the Levitical unclean status. Common extensions: Gentiles/pagans, gluttony/sensuality, demonic association (Gadarene swine), and the ravaging boar as an enemy. One response (B) lists a minority reading of hypocrisy based on the pig's divided hoof without chewing the cud.
book_summary: Swine are an unclean beast signifying a people or kingdom bearing the outward covenant sign without the inward work (parted hoof, no cud-chewing) — hypocritical religionists who trample the holy and return to uncleanness after washing; corporately, the Synagogue of Satan, those who say they are Jews and are not (Rev 2:9; 3:9).
consensus_core_identification: Uncleanness/impurity and the profane or apostate person who despises or returns from holy things.
book_core_identification: A hypocritical covenant people — outwardly religious but inwardly unclean — corporately identified as the false-Jewish Synagogue of Satan.
boundary_disagreement: The consensus applies swine broadly to any unclean, profane, or unreceptive persons, and commonly to Gentiles/pagans as covenant outsiders. The book narrows the referent to a specific corporate body: professing covenant members whose sign is only outward (the divided-hoof-without-cud emblem), culminating in the 'Synagogue of Satan.' This effectively inverts the common Gentile-outsider extension — swine are false insiders, not pagan outsiders — while retaining the trampling-the-holy (Matt 7:6) and washed-sow apostasy (2 Pet 2:22) cases. Generic sensuality, gluttony, demonic, and boar-enemy applications are dropped.
material_contradiction: None at the core: uncleanness, hypocrisy, and return to filth are all within the consensus field (B's hoof/cud hypocrisy alternative and the widespread apostasy reading). The tension with the Gentile-identification alternative is a reclassification at the boundary, not a replacement of the central unclean/profane category.
rationale: The book preserves the consensus's central category — the swine as the emblem of uncleanness, hypocritical profession, trampling the holy, and reversion to filth — but materially sharpens its extension into a specific corporate referent (a people/kingdom; the Synagogue of Satan of Rev 2:9/3:9). This is real boundary disagreement (false covenant claimants rather than generic sinners or Gentiles) without contradicting the unclean/profane core, so REFINED fits. It is not NOVEL because the hypocrisy-from-anatomy reading appears as a listed minority alternative and the apostasy reading is common; not DIVERGENT because no consensus identification must be rejected as false of the same texts.
strongest_objection: The specific corporate identification with the Synagogue of Satan (Rev 2:9; 3:9) — a group nowhere linked to swine in Scripture — appears in no consensus response or alternative, so one could argue the book's true core (false Jews as a body) is NOVEL rather than a refinement; the cited texts connect swine to hypocrisy only by an inferential chain (Lev 11:7 anatomy + Matt 23 + Rom 2), not by explicit textual linkage.
